title: Eval traffic-weighted regression triage, degradation buckets, and progressive rollforward PRD
creator: Maya Singh
description: Purpose: Define a pragmatic, actionable PRD that specifies how Optimize will detect, triage, and respond to model regressions discovered via automated evals and A/B rollouts. This PRD covers: (1) design of representative prompt sets (canary + production-weighted), (2) a degradation bucket taxonomy aligned to business and SLO impact, (3) statically defined regression thresholds and statistical tests, (4) A/B gating criteria and minimum sample rules, (5) automated rollback triggers and a progressive rollforward playbook, and (6) dashboards/alerts required for on-call teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary prompt set: 5k unique prompts generated across 10 cohorts (safety, hallucination-prone, latency-sensitive, high-cost, long-context, FAQ, legal templates, multi-turn dialogs, embeddings+generation combos, and customer-critical flows). Canary must run at 0.5% traffic by default.

2) Composite quality metric defined and computed: weighted aggregation of (utility_score, safety_score, factuality_score, instruction_adherence) normalized 0-100. Baseline computed per model-version and stored for 90 days.

3) Regression detection: an observed drop in composite quality >= 0.75 points AND p-value < 0.01 (two-sided bootstrap of paired samples) with minimum paired sample N >= 1000 triggers 'actionable' alert.

4) A/B gating: candidate must show non-inferior safety (no increase in safety failures) and either a statistically significant improvement in cost-per-token or non-inferior utility at alpha=0.01 with minimum 5k requests per cohort and sequential testing with pre-specified stopping rules.

5) Rollback triggers include (a) safety failure rate increase > 0.15% absolute over baseline, (b) increase in customer error reports > 0.1% of calls concentrated in last 60 minutes, (c) 99th percentile latency > SLO + 30% for 30m window, or (d) composite quality drop > 2.0 points. Any trigger requires an automated failover to the previous stable variant and immediate incident page creation.

6) Progressive rollforward automation implemented: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% windows with automated gating checks and manual approval for >25% progression. Canary windows must be at least 24h for first two steps and 48h at 25% unless traffic-scarce.

7) Dashboards: model-version time series for composite_quality, safety_score, factuality, latency p50/p95/p99, token_cost, error_rate, and customer-reported issues. All must have historical baselines and rolling deltas. Alerts must integrate with Ops paging.

8) Playbook: documented triage steps, owner rotations, rollback verification steps, postmortem template, and follow-up remediation pathways. Playbook must be accessible in Confluence and linked from the Console rollout UI.
prompt_set_spec: Canary set composition: 5k prompts stratified by traffic weights: top-50 customer templates (40%), open-ended web-style prompts (20%), safety-stress prompts (10%), long-context continuations (10%), multi-turn dialogues (10%), low-latency/short-prompt samples (10%).
Sampling cadence: weekly re-sampling to avoid dataset staleness; immutable snapshot for each canary run stored with commit hash and evaluator config.
Labeling & ground truth: small subset (500 prompts) labeled by human raters for calibration; inter-rater agreement target KR: Cohen's kappa >= 0.6.
Seed variants: include adversarial prompt subset for safety regressions and hallucination checks; these live in a locked 'safety-canary' partition.
regression_thresholds: Minor degradation: composite_quality drop between 0.25 - 0.75 points (investigate; non-blocking), requires owner notification and a short-run rollback candidate audit.
Actionable degradation: composite_quality drop >= 0.75 points AND p<0.01 with N>=1000 (Blocker for canary progression; require mitigation plan within 4 business hours).
Critical regression: composite_quality drop >= 2.0 points OR safety failure increase > 0.15% absolute OR hallucination spike > 0.5% absolute (immediate automated rollback and incident declared).
Latency & reliability thresholds: 99th pctl latency > SLO*1.3 for a sustained 30m window OR error_rate increase > 3x baseline for 15m triggers urgent rollback.
Cost thresholds: token_cost per response increases > 25% relative to baseline for sustained 24h period triggers investigation (no immediate rollback unless combined with quality degradation).
ab_criteria: Minimum traffic per arm: 5k requests per arm for main cohorts; for low-volume cohorts require pooled analysis with at least 2k per arm and adjusted alpha.
Statistical test: two-sided bootstrap on paired metrics where applicable; otherwise use Chi-squared for binary safety signals. Use Benjamini-Hochberg correction across multiple cohorts/signals.
Stopping rules: sequential analysis with alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) and pre-registered maximum-duration of 14 days per experiment.

Decision boundaries: require non-inferiority on safety (margin 0.1% absolute) AND either improvement in unit-cost or non-inferior composite_quality. Where conflicting signals exist, default to safety-first and require PM approval to proceed.
rollback_triggers: Automated rollback if any Critical regression threshold is met.
Automatic pause of rollforward if Actionable degradation is detected in the canary window (system will reduce traffic back to previous stable variant and page on-call).
Manual rollback paths: on-call engineer can trigger immediate rollback with audit log and reason code; Product/Eng lead to convene within 2 hours for remediation plan.
Post-rollback verification: traffic must be routed to previous stable variant and composite_quality must return to within 0.25 points of baseline before considering re-deploy.
rollforward_strategy: Phase 0: Local validation and CI tests (model inference correctness, unit tests, smoke tests).
Phase 1: Internal canary on synthetic traffic (simulated 24h equivalence) to validate metrics pipeline.
Phase 2: 1% production canary (24h window) with automated checks; if pass -> Phase 3.
Phase 3: 5% production canary (24h window) with automated and manual check; PM/Eng review required before Phase 4.
Phase 4: 25% staged rollout (48h window) with manual gating; require no Actionable or Critical regressions and Ops approval to proceed to 100%.
Phase 5: 100% release with monitoring and 72h heightened observation; any critical regression during this period triggers immediate rollback.
monitoring_signals: Composite_quality (primary), safety_score, factuality_rate, instruction_adherence, token_cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error_rate, server_cpu/gpu utilization, internal QA feedback, customer incident rate.
Signal provenance tagging: every alert includes contributors (canary prompt subset, production cohort, time window) and sample IDs for quick repro and human review.
Drift monitoring: distribution shift detection for prompt length, token usage, and prompt types compared to baseline. Alerts when K-L divergence > threshold.
